title: Does 4SUM survive the thin-product attack?
W: Solve 4SUM on n integers of poly(n) magnitude in O(n^{2-eps}) time, or 3SUM-Indexing with S space and T query time where S*T = O(n^{2-eps}); alternatively prove that any algorithm built from AVW-style thin rectangular product subroutines plus fine-grained self-reductions cannot beat n^{ceil(k/2)} for k=4.
M: Yes: the k-SUM hierarchy (and the 3SUM-Indexing data-structure lower bounds) fall, and the n^{ceil(k/2)} conjecture is wrong. A barrier: explains why 3SUM fell but 4SUM did not (lack of self-reductions), and makes 4SUM the natural replacement hardness source.
why: AVW explicitly could not improve k-SUM/k-XOR for k>=4 or 3SUM-Indexing, blaming lack of fine-grained self-reductions. These are now the main surviving additive-combinatorics hypotheses in fine-grained complexity.
status_notes: 3SUM refuted (AVW, arXiv:2610.06783, Oct 2026 preprint); AVW list k-SUM/k-XOR k>=4 and the 3SUM-Indexing conjecture as NOT refuted and open. Majdoddin (arXiv:2610.17420) extends to 3SUM over abelian groups, not to 4SUM.
refs: Alman, Vassilevska Williams, Truly Subquadratic 3SUM and Truly Subcubic APSP via Triangles in Sparse Lopsided Graphs, arXiv:2610.06783 (Oct 2026)
Majdoddin, Thin matrix products up to D<=N^0.172 and lossless reductions for 3SUM, Exact Triangle and APSP, arXiv:2610.17420 (Oct 2026)
Goldstein, Kopelowitz, Lewenstein, Porat, How hard is it to find (honest) witnesses?, ESA 2016 (3SUM-Indexing)
issues: 3SUM refuted (AVW, arXiv:2610.06783, Oct 2026 preprint); AVW list k-SUM/k-XOR k>=4 and the 3SUM-Indexing conjecture as NOT refuted and open. Majdoddin (arXiv:2610.17420) extends to 3SUM over abelian groups, not to 4SUM.

assumption: Sparse triangle / k-Clique-type hypotheses (Patrascu balanced instances)
title: All-Edges Sparse Triangle below m^{4/3} on balanced instances
W: Solve All-Edges Sparse Triangle (for each of m edges, report whether it is in a triangle) in O(m^{4/3-eps}) time on general (balanced) sparse graphs, or derive an m^{4/3-o(1)} lower bound from a hypothesis that survives AVW (e.g. 4SUM, OV/SETH, or combinatorial BMM).
M: Yes: kills Patrascu-style lower bounds for dynamic and data-structure problems that go through balanced instances (set-disjointness, dynamic reachability lower bounds). No: re-grounds the m^{4/3} barrier on a still-standing assumption.
why: AVW handle only lopsided instances and explicitly leave Patrascu's balanced instances open; dozens of dynamic lower bounds rest on m^{4/3}.
status_notes: m^{4/3} lower bounds (Patrascu STOC 2010; Kopelowitz-Pettie-Porat SODA 2016) came from 3SUM, now refuted (AVW arXiv:2610.06783, Oct 2026). AVW state balanced sparse instances are not addressed. Best known upper bound O(m^{2omega/(omega+1)}).
refs: Alman, Vassilevska Williams, Truly Subquadratic 3SUM and Truly Subcubic APSP via Triangles in Sparse Lopsided Graphs, arXiv:2610.06783 (Oct 2026)
Patrascu, Towards polynomial lower bounds for dynamic problems, STOC 2010
Kopelowitz, Pettie, Porat, Higher lower bounds from the 3SUM conjecture, SODA 2016
issues: m^{4/3} lower bounds (Patrascu STOC 2010; Kopelowitz-Pettie-Porat SODA 2016) came from 3SUM, now refuted (AVW arXiv:2610.06783, Oct 2026). AVW state balanced sparse instances are not addressed. Best known upper bound O(m^{2omega/(omega+1)}).

title: 2^{Omega(n)} hardness of Euclidean SVP under ETH
W: Show that approximate SVP in the l_2 norm (some constant gamma>1) has no 2^{o(n)}-time algorithm unless (randomized) ETH fails; or identify an obstruction (e.g. for the Z^n-based gadget) showing the l_p, p>2 technique cannot reach p=2.
M: Yes: grounds the concrete security of lattice cryptography (l_2 SVP) on ETH rather than Gap-ETH. Obstruction: explains why l_2 is special, complementing known barriers for SETH-hardness of CVP in even norms.
why: Stated as Open Problem 1 (p in [1,2], specifically p=2) in the ICALP 2026 paper; the most cryptographically relevant case.
status_notes: Aggarwal-Gupta-Morolia-Zhang (ICALP 2026) prove ETH-hardness for CVP_p (all p>=1) and SVP_p (p>2); p in [1,2] incl. p=2 left open. Earlier SVP_2 2^{Omega(n)} hardness required Gap-ETH-type assumptions.
refs: Aggarwal, Gupta, Morolia, Zhang, Mind the Gap? Not for SVP Hardness under ETH!, ICALP 2026, arXiv:2504.02695
issues: Aggarwal-Gupta-Morolia-Zhang (ICALP 2026) prove ETH-hardness for CVP_p (all p>=1) and SVP_p (p>2); p in [1,2] incl. p=2 left open. Earlier SVP_2 2^{Omega(n)} hardness required Gap-ETH-type assumptions.

assumption: Circuit lower bounds underlying derandomization (E needs exponential circuits)
title: From S_2E to E^NP: near-maximum circuit lower bounds
W: Prove E^NP is not contained in SIZE[2^n/n] (or even SIZE[2^{epsilon n}] for some eps>0 infinitely often); equivalently, put Range Avoidance in FP^NP for the relevant circuit classes, improving Li's FS_2^P algorithm.
M: Yes: an unconditional exponential lower bound one level lower than currently known, strengthening hardness-vs-randomness inputs (e.g. derandomization of AM / prBPP in P^NP-type classes). Barrier/relativization result: shows the symmetric-alternation step of Chen-Hirahara-Ren/Li is essential.
why: The 2023-24 breakthrough reached S_2E; E^NP is the natural next class and is explicitly the target of the range-avoidance program.
status_notes: Chen-Hirahara-Ren (STOC 2024) and Li (STOC 2024) proved S_2E needs 2^n/n circuits via FS_2^P range avoidance; Hitchcock (arXiv:2605.03306, 2026) shows such languages are comeager in S_2E. E^NP case remains open; BPP=P still conditional.
refs: Chen, Hirahara, Ren, Symmetric exponential time requires near-maximum circuit size, STOC 2024, arXiv:2309.12912
Li, Symmetric exponential time requires near-maximum circuit size: simplified, truly uniform, STOC 2024, arXiv:2310.17762
Hitchcock, Exponential-size circuit complexity is comeager in symmetric exponential time, arXiv:2605.03306
issues: Chen-Hirahara-Ren (STOC 2024) and Li (STOC 2024) proved S_2E needs 2^n/n circuits via FS_2^P range avoidance; Hitchcock (arXiv:2605.03306, 2026) shows such languages are comeager in S_2E. E^NP case remains open; BPP=P still conditional.

assumption: Katz–Sarnak random-matrix symmetry types for low-lying zeros (GRH-based)
title: One-level density of quadratic Dirichlet L-functions beyond support (−2,2)
W: Under GRH, the low-lying zeros of L(s,χ_d) for quadratic characters are known to follow the symplectic random-matrix law only for test functions whose Fourier transform is supported in (−2,2). Go beyond 2.
M: For the family of real primitive characters $\chi_{8d}$, $d$ odd squarefree, $X<d\le 2X$, and even Schwartz $\phi$ with $\operatorname{supp}\hat\phi\subset(-\sigma,\sigma)$, prove under GRH that $\frac1{|\mathcal F|}\sum_d\sum_{\gamma_d}\phi\!\big(\gamma_d\frac{\log X}{2\pi}\big)\to\int\phi(x)\big(1-\frac{\sin 2\pi x}{2\pi x}\big)dx$ for some $\sigma>2$.
why: Support beyond 2 is the classic test of the symplectic prediction in its non-trivial range and would give better nonvanishing proportions for L(1/2,χ_d). For the averaged family of all Dirichlet characters, Drappeau–Pratt–Radziwiłł got past 2 unconditionally (to 2+50/1093) using large-sieve and dispersion input. The question is whether analogous input exists for the thinner quadratic family.
status_notes: Özlük–Snyder: support (−2,2) under GRH for quadratic family; Rubinstein for n-level. Drappeau–Pratt–Radziwiłł (ANT 2023): beyond 2 (to 2+50/1093) for all primitive characters with conductor in [Q/2,Q]. I found no extension past 2 for the quadratic family; ratios-conjecture computations predict the answer.

assumption: Stability of Gaussian elimination with pivoting (growth factor assumptions in numerical linear algebra)
title: Is the complete-pivoting growth factor superlinear?
W: Numerical analysts long assumed the worst-case growth factor of Gaussian elimination with complete pivoting is at most n. This was refuted: it is at least 1.0045n for n>10, and the limsup of g_n/n is at least 3.317. Decide whether g_n grows faster than every linear function, or better, like n^{1+δ}.
M: Let $g_n=\sup_A \max_{i,j,k}|a^{(k)}_{ij}|/\max_{ij}|a_{ij}|$ over real nonsingular $n\times n$ $A$ under complete pivoting. Known: $g_n\ge 1.0045n$ ($n>10$), $\limsup g_n/n\ge 3.317$ (Edelman–Urschel 2024), $g_n\le n^{0.2079\ln n+0.91}$ (Bisain–Edelman–Urschel 2024). Prove $g_n/n\to\infty$ along a subsequence, or $g_n\ge n^{1+\delta}$ infinitely often, or $g_n=O(n)$.
why: Complete pivoting is the textbook 'provably safe' variant of Gaussian elimination. The gap between linear lower bounds and a quasi-polynomial upper bound has stood since Wilkinson (1961), apart from one 2024 improvement. Superlinear growth would mean the classical stability folklore is false asymptotically, while O(n) would vindicate it.
status_notes: Folklore conjecture g_n≤n refuted for n>10 (Edelman–Urschel 2024, arXiv 2303.04892; Gould 1991 for n=13 in floating point). Their numerics give g_100>3n, and they suggest g_n/n→∞. Upper bound improved for the first time since Wilkinson: n^{0.2079 ln n+0.91} (arXiv 2312.00994).
